title: Bandwidth-Effective DRAM Cache for GPU s with Storage-Class Memory
problem: GPUs have limited HBM capacity for memory-oversubscribed workloads. Storage-Class Memory offers higher capacity but higher latency and lower bandwidth than DRAM, requiring an effective DRAM cache design to bridge the performance gap.
motivation: Extending GPU memory capacity with SCM enables larger datasets and improves performance for memory-intensive applications.
method: The paper proposes an SCM-aware DRAM cache with: (1) a bypass policy that avoids caching low-utility data based on GPU access patterns, (2) a Configurable Tag Cache (CTC) repurposing L2 cache to reduce DRAM probe traffic, (3) Aggregated Metadata-In-Last-column (AMIL) organization co-locating tags in a single column while preserving ECC, and (4) SCM throttling and SLC/MLC mode adaptation.
key_novelty: Aggregated Metadata-In-Last-column (AMIL) DRAM cache organization that co-locates all cacheline tags in a single column to minimize probe traffic while maintaining full ECC protection.
contributions: SCM-aware DRAM cache bypass policy for GPU memory access characteristics
Configurable Tag Cache (CTC) design to reduce DRAM probe traffic with adjustable L2 capacity
Aggregated Metadata-In-Last-column (AMIL) organization with full ECC retention versus TAD
Heterogeneous Memory Stack (HMS) architecture combining stacked DRAM and SCM
baselines: prior DRAM cache implementations with TAD organization
primary_theme: GPU memory capacity extension via DRAM-SCM hierarchy optimization
